Looking at the remaining results, the lower alpha values and DSIR are falling further behind—DSIR specifically underperforms our binary approach by about 7 percentage points on both metrics. GPU is currently at 83% utilization running exp-015, which is extracting embeddings from Pythia-1.4B as the first of three models.

Now I need to update the experiment registry to mark exp-006 as complete with its metrics, remove its cron job, add exp-015 as running with a new cron, and then prepare the full results table for the Director before updating the report.

        "filePath": "/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_7/projects/gen-depth-contamination/docs/paper/method.tex",
        "content": "\\section{Method}\n\\label{sec:method}\n\n\\begin{figure*}[t]\n\\centering\n\\includegraphics[width=\\textwidth]{figures/pipeline.pdf}\n\\caption{Generational depth estimation pipeline. Seed documents are recursively passed through a generation operator $G_\\delta$ to produce a depth chain. Statistical features are fed to the OBD-LightGBM classifier for depth prediction.}\n\\label{fig:pipeline}\n\\end{figure*}\n\n\\subsection{Problem Formulation}\n\\label{sec:formulation}\n\nA generation operator $G_\\delta$ (LLM + decoding strategy $\\delta$) produces successive generations $X \\to Y_1 \\to \\cdots \\to Y_K$, where $Y_k = G_\\delta(Y_{k-1})$ and $Y_0 \\triangleq X$ (Figure~\\ref{fig:pipeline}).\nThis sequence forms a Markov chain.\nBy the Data Processing Inequality, $I(X; Y_1) \\geq I(X; Y_2) \\geq \\cdots \\geq 0$: the original signal degrades monotonically.\nTogether with Markov chain convergence, this guarantees a finite $\\Ktheory$ beyond which adjacent generations are indistinguishable.\n\nWe define the operational lower bound:\n\\begin{equation}\n  \\Kempirical = \\max\\{k : \\text{CI}_{\\text{lower}}^{95\\%}(\\auc_{k,k+1}) > \\theta\\},\n  \\label{eq:kstar}\n\\end{equation}\nwhere $\\theta = 0.60$ is justified by the permutation null distribution (95th percentile $< 0.55$ across all configurations; bootstrap: 1{,}000 resamples).\n\n\\subsection{Features and Classifier}\n\\label{sec:features}\n\nEach document is characterized by a 15-dimensional feature vector spanning four groups: \\emph{surprisal moments} (mean, std, skewness, kurtosis; 4~dims), \\emph{surprisal derivatives} (mean and std of first- and second-order differences, plus first-order skewness; 5~dims), \\emph{vocabulary diversity} (type-token ratio, hapax legomena ratio, self-BLEU; 3~dims), and \\emph{frequency tail statistics} (frequency kurtosis, entropy, rare token fraction; 3~dims).\nAll features are computed from token-level surprisal values via an external scorer model (full definitions in Table~\\ref{tab:s5_features}, Appendix).\nHand-crafted features enable cross-generator transfer without retraining and permit attribution of discriminative power to specific text properties.\n\nWe use \\emph{Ordinal Binary Decomposition} (OBD), decomposing the $(K{+}1)$-class problem into $K$ cumulative binary sub-classifiers, each estimating $P(\\text{depth} > k \\mid \\mathbf{x})$ via LightGBM (hyperparameters in Table~\\ref{tab:s6_lgbm_params}).\nOBD achieves lower MAE than multiclass LightGBM (e.g., 0.984 vs.\\ 1.016 on Qwen-rewrite) while maintaining superior pairwise $\\auc$ (mean 0.6095 vs.\\ 0.4883 for ordinal logistic regression).\n\n\\subsection{Experimental Setup}\n\\label{sec:experimental_setup}\n\nWe evaluate four configurations spanning three model families (Table~\\ref{tab:setup}): Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (rewrite and continuation modes), Pythia-1.4B and OLMo-1B (continuation).\nEach uses 5{,}000 C4 seeds truncated to 256 tokens, recursively generated for $K{=}5$ iterations (30{,}000 documents per configuration).\nDefault decoding: nucleus $p{=}0.95$, $T{=}1.0$; decoding ablation covers greedy, $T{=}0.7$, and $T{=}1.2$.\nContinuation mode truncates seeds to 128 tokens and extends to 256; rewrite mode paraphrases the full text.\nEvaluation: 5-fold GroupKFold cross-validation grouped by seed document; pairwise $\\auc$ as primary metric.\n\n\\begin{table}[t]\n\\centering\n\\small\n\\caption{Experimental configurations.}\n\\label{tab:setup}\n\\begin{tabular}{llcc}\n\\toprule\n\\textbf{Config} & \\textbf{Model} & \\textbf{Mode} & $N$ \\\\\n\\midrule\nQwen-rw   & Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct & Rewrite & 5{,}000 \\\\\nQwen-cont & Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct & Continuation & 5{,}000 \\\\\nPythia    & Pythia-1.4B            & Continuation & 5{,}000 \\\\\nOLMo      & OLMo-1B               & Continuation & 5{,}000 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n",
        "numLines": 61,
        "startLine": 1,
        "totalLines": 61
      }
    },

        "content": "\\section{Experiments}\n\\label{sec:experiments}\n\nWe evaluate generational depth estimation on four model configurations:\nPythia-1.4B and OLMo-1B in continuation mode, and Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct in both rewrite and continuation modes.\nAll experiments use the OBD-LightGBM classifier with the 15-dimensional feature set (Section~\\ref{sec:method}), with 5{,}000 texts per depth level (generations 0--5).\n\n%% ====================================================================\n\\subsection{$\\Kempirical = 2$ Across All Configurations}\n\\label{sec:kstar_boundary}\n\n\\begin{table*}[t]\n\\centering\n\\small\n\\caption{Pairwise $\\auc$ for adjacent depth pairs with bootstrap 95\\% CIs and permutation $p$-values for boundary rows.\n$\\Kempirical = 2$ requires 1v2 $\\text{CI}_\\text{low} > \\theta{=}0.60$ and 2v3 $\\text{CI}_\\text{high} < \\theta$.}\n\\label{tab:kstar_ci}\n\\begin{tabular}{lcccccccc}\n\\toprule\n & \\multicolumn{2}{c}{Qwen-rw} & \\multicolumn{2}{c}{Pythia} & \\multicolumn{2}{c}{OLMo} & \\multicolumn{2}{c}{Qwen-cont} \\\\\n\\cmidrule(lr){2-3}\\cmidrule(lr){4-5}\\cmidrule(lr){6-7}\\cmidrule(lr){8-9}\n & $\\auc$ & 95\\% CI & $\\auc$ & 95\\% CI & $\\auc$ & 95\\% CI & $\\auc$ & 95\\% CI \\\\\n\\midrule\n0v1 & .9956 & & .9932 & & .9970 & & .9971 & \\\\\n1v2 & .6955 & [.686,\\,.704]\\rlap{$^*$} & .6539 & [.645,\\,.663]\\rlap{$^*$} & .6145 & [.605,\\,.625]\\rlap{$^*$} & .6112 & [.602,\\,.621]\\rlap{$^*$} \\\\\n2v3 & .5893 & [.580,\\,.599] & .5514 & [.542,\\,.563] & .5496 & [.540,\\,.560] & .5609 & [.551,\\,.571] \\\\\n3v4 & .5435 & & .5152 & & .5091 & & .5409 & \\\\\n4v5 & .5340 & & .5136 & & .5045 & & .5141 & \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\multicolumn{9}{l}{\\footnotesize $^*$Permutation $p = 0.002$ for all 1v2 comparisons.}\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table*}\n\n\\begin{figure}[t]\n\\centering\n\\includegraphics[width=\\columnwidth]{figures/fig2_auc_decay.pdf}\n\\caption{Pairwise $\\auc$ decay across depth pairs for model-mode configurations (solid) and decoding strategies (dashed). The horizontal dashed line marks $\\theta = 0.60$.}\n\\label{fig:auc_decay}\n\\end{figure}\n\nTable~\\ref{tab:kstar_ci} and Figure~\\ref{fig:auc_decay} show a consistent pattern: 0v1 discrimination is near-perfect ($\\auc > 0.99$), followed by a sharp ${\\sim}$30\\,pp drop at 1v2 ($\\auc$: 0.6112--0.6955), with 2v3 falling below $\\theta$ (0.5496--0.5893) and deeper pairs converging toward chance.\nAll four 1v2 CI lower bounds exceed $\\theta$ (most marginal: Qwen-continuation at 0.6015), and all four 2v3 CI upper bounds fall below $\\theta$, with permutation $p = 0.002$ for all boundary comparisons.\nThis establishes $\\Kempirical = 2$ as a consistent boundary across all tested configurations.\n\nThe 1v2 $\\auc$ varies across models: Qwen-rewrite (0.6955) $>$ Pythia (0.6539) $>$ OLMo (0.6145) $\\approx$ Qwen-continuation (0.6112).\nThe spread due to generation mode within a single model ($\\Delta = 8.4$\\,pp) exceeds the spread across models in the same mode ($\\Delta = 3.9$\\,pp), suggesting generation protocol is a stronger determinant of detectability than model identity.\n\nAt $\\theta = 0.55$, $\\Kempirical = 3$ uniformly; at $\\theta = 0.65$, continuation modes drop to $\\Kempirical = 1$ while rewrite retains $\\Kempirical = 2$; at $\\theta = 0.70$, $\\Kempirical = 1$ universally.\nAll four decoding configurations (greedy, nucleus, $T{=}0.70$, $T{=}1.2$) likewise yield $\\Kempirical = 2$ at $\\theta = 0.60$, with 1v2 $\\auc$ in $[0.6866, 0.7039]$ (Table~\\ref{tab:s2_decoding}).\n\n%% ====================================================================\n\\subsection{Cross-Model Transfer}\n\\label{sec:transfer}\n\n\\begin{figure}[t]\n\\centering\n\\includegraphics[width=0.85\\columnwidth]{figures/fig3_transfer_heatmap.pdf}\n\\caption{Cross-model transfer heatmap (6-class ordinal accuracy). Pythia$\\leftrightarrow$OLMo achieves 90--92\\% retention; Qwen-rewrite$\\to$continuation-mode models: 61--63\\%.}\n\\label{fig:transfer_heatmap}\n\\end{figure}\n\nFigure~\\ref{fig:transfer_heatmap} shows the transfer accuracy matrix (full matrix in Table~\\ref{tab:s1_transfer}).\nContinuation-mode transfer is high: Pythia$\\leftrightarrow$OLMo retains 90--92\\% of within-model accuracy, Qwen-cont$\\leftrightarrow$Pythia 84--85\\%, and Qwen-cont$\\leftrightarrow$OLMo 80--85\\%.\nAt the 0v1 boundary, cross-model $\\auc$ exceeds 0.96 for all pairs.\nThese retention rates suggest a large text-intrinsic component of the depth signal.\n\nQwen-rewrite classifiers transfer poorly (61--63\\% retention to Pythia/OLMo), confirming reliance on mode-specific artifacts.\nCross-mode transfer is asymmetric: continuation$\\to$rewrite retains 89\\% while rewrite$\\to$continuation retains 82\\%, indicating that continuation-mode features form a generalizable subset.\n\n%% ====================================================================\n\\subsection{Feature Degradation Ordering}\n\\label{sec:feature_degradation}\n\n\\begin{table*}[t]\n\\centering\n\\small\n\\caption{Top-3 features by single-feature $\\auc$ ranking. Bold: shared across all continuation-mode models. Spearman $\\rho$ (continuation pairs): Pythia--OLMo 0.95, Pythia--Qwen-cont 0.91, OLMo--Qwen-cont 0.85.}\n\\label{tab:top_features}\n\\begin{tabular}{cllll}\n\\toprule\nRank & Pythia & OLMo & Qwen-rw & Qwen-cont \\\\\n\\midrule\n1 & \\textbf{\\texttt{surp\\_d1\\_std}} & \\textbf{\\texttt{surp\\_std}} & \\texttt{freq\\_entropy} & \\textbf{\\texttt{surp\\_d1\\_std}} \\\\\n2 & \\textbf{\\texttt{surp\\_d2\\_std}} & \\textbf{\\texttt{surp\\_d1\\_std}} & \\textbf{\\texttt{surp\\_std}} & \\textbf{\\texttt{surp\\_std}} \\\\\n3 & \\textbf{\\texttt{surp\\_std}} & \\textbf{\\texttt{surp\\_d2\\_std}} & \\textbf{\\texttt{surp\\_d1\\_std}} & \\textbf{\\texttt{surp\\_d2\\_std}} \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table*}\n\nAmong continuation-mode models, single-feature $\\auc$ rankings are highly correlated ($\\rho \\geq 0.85$; Table~\\ref{tab:top_features}).\nThe top-3 features---\\texttt{surp\\_d1\\_std}, \\texttt{surp\\_std}, \\texttt{surp\\_d2\\_std}---are shared across all three families, all measuring surprisal variability.\nThis shared ordering suggests a common mechanism: each generation step smooths the token-level surprisal landscape.\nQwen-rewrite diverges, with \\texttt{freq\\_entropy} as its top feature---corroborating the cross-model transfer findings.\nA limitation is that depth-pair-level agreement weakens ($\\tau \\approx 0.37$ at 1v2), indicating per-feature contributions at the boundary vary across models.\n\n%% ====================================================================\n\\subsection{Generation Mode and Neural Probe}\n\\label{sec:generation_mode}\n\nWithin Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, rewrite mode yields 1v2 $\\auc = 0.6955$ versus continuation's $0.6112$ ($\\Delta = +8.4$\\,pp).\nThe amplified detectability reflects instruction-following artifacts that are discriminable but mode-specific rather than text-intrinsic, as confirmed by the poor cross-model transfer of rewrite-mode classifiers (61--63\\% vs.\\ 80--92\\% for continuation).\nContinuation mode is therefore recommended as the canonical condition for cross-model comparisons.\n\n\\paragraph{Neural probe.}\nReplacing hand-crafted features with frozen Qwen2.5-1.5B hidden states (1536-dim, MLP probe; Table~\\ref{tab:s7_neural_probe}), the 2v3 $\\auc$ reaches 0.6195 (vs.\\ 0.5609 with 15D features), yielding $\\Kempirical^{\\text{neural}} = 3$.\nThis confirms that $\\Kempirical = 2$ is a representation-dependent lower bound: the 15D feature set does not saturate the available depth signal.\nHowever, the result is preliminary (single dataset, marginal: $+$1.95\\,pp above $\\theta$) and awaits cross-model validation on Pythia and OLMo (Table~\\ref{tab:neural_probe_crossmodel}).\n\n\\begin{table}[t]\n\\centering\n\\footnotesize\n\\caption{Neural probe pairwise $\\auc$ (frozen-encoder MLP). Pythia/OLMo results pending.}\n\\label{tab:neural_probe_crossmodel}\n\\begin{tabular}{lccccc}\n\\toprule\n\\textbf{Model} & \\textbf{0v1} & \\textbf{1v2} & \\textbf{2v3} & \\textbf{3v4} & $\\Kempirical^{\\text{neural}}$ \\\\\n\\midrule\nQwen-1.5B & 0.987 & 0.698 & 0.620 & 0.593 & 3 \\\\\nPythia-1.4B & \\textit{--} & \\textit{--} & \\textit{--} & \\textit{--} & \\textit{--} \\\\\nOLMo-1B & \\textit{--} & \\textit{--} & \\textit{--} & \\textit{--} & \\textit{--} \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n",
